+# Fixture trails
+
+Small, hand-checked trails for the behaviour tests (web-testing.spec C3). Each folder is a repo in
+pieces, replayed by `replay.mjs` into a fresh git repo, so the trail compiler is tested on git at a ref,
+the same way it reads the real one. The live `docs/trace/` is never a test input.
+
+## The form
+
+```text
+<name>/
+  README.md      what it proves, what it is cut from, and the expected check label
+  base/          the repo before the node: docs/requirements.md, docs/plans/active/<plan>.dag.yaml
+  commits.json   { date, branch, commits: [{ id, subject, trailers, files }] }, in order
+  files/         the content each commit adds, by repo path
+  trail/         docs/trace/<plan>/<node>/: loop, activity, verdicts, findings, written last
+```
+
+- **Replay:** `base/` is committed and becomes `origin/main`. Each commit is made on `branch` with its
+  trailers (`--allow-empty` when it lists no files), all at `date`. Then `trail/` is written, uncommitted,
+  as at `/feature`'s trace step, where `render-trace check` runs. `replay(fixture, dir, { trail: false })`
+  stops before it.
+- **SHAs:** `{{c3}}` in any file becomes commit `c3`'s SHA, and `{{c3:7}}` its short form. A file only
+  names commits made before it is placed.
+- **`.fixture`:** a path ending `.fixture` loses the suffix when placed. Test files carry it, so this
+  repo's own rule-tag walker never counts a fixture's `SELL-1 · ` titles as real markers.
+- **Checked by hand and by the real tool:** each README's label is what `render-trace check build F1`
+  printed on the replayed repo when the fixture was made. A compiler test asserts its own fields from the
+  README's facts, not from re-running the harness.
+
+## The fixtures
+
+| Folder | Proves |
+|---|---|
+| `complete/` | A clean node: red, stub, green, QA, one PASS pair, every gate ok |
+| `incomplete/` | An incomplete trail is shown with every reason, never as clean (DATA-4) |
+| `fail-and-fix/` | A reviewer FAIL, its findings, a red test and a fix carrying `Fixes-Finding`, then a PASS |
+
+A test that needs a case none of these has (a git-only node, an in-flight node, a malformed line, a
+privacy hit, a lost verdict) adds a fixture in its red commit, in this form.

+# complete
+
+One feature node, `build/F1` (Sell), with rules SELL-1 and SELL-2, run once, cleanly. Cut from the shape
+of the real `build/F1` trail: the same event names, verdict envelope and trailers, with two rules and
+five commits.
+
+- **Commits** (on `feature/build/F1`): c0 plan status (main), c1 red (tester, `Rule: SELL-1, SELL-2`,
+  `TDD: red`, adds the acceptance spec with one `SELL-1 · ` and one `SELL-2 · ` title), c2 stub
+  (builder), c3 green (builder), c4 QA script (tester, no `TDD`).
+- **Loop:** setup, state, `gate.red` (expect fail, ok), `gate.stub`, `pause1`, `gate.green`, both A1
+  verdicts, `gate.integrate`. Attempt 1 throughout.
+- **Verdicts:** A1 reviewer PASS covering SELL-1 and SELL-2, A1 security PASS, both at c3.
+- **Activity:** one record per commit, with its SHA and subject.
+- **QA:** a step row for each rule.
+
+**Expected:** `render-trace check build F1` → exit 0, `OK`. Both rules have red c1 before green c3,
+a test marker each, and a QA step; there are no findings and no steers.

+// Replays a fixture trail into a fresh git repo (web-testing.spec C3; the form is in README.md beside this).
+// The base becomes origin/main; each commit in commits.json is made on feature/<plan>/<node> with its
+// trailers; then the trail files are written, uncommitted, as at the trace step. {{cN}} and {{cN:7}} in any
+// file become commit cN's SHA. A path ending .fixture loses the suffix, so the repo's own rule-tag walker
+// never counts a fixture's test titles.
+//
+//   import { replay } from './replay.mjs';  const { root, shas } = replay('<fixture dir>', '<empty dir>');
+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { cpSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { dirname, join, relative } from 'node:path';
+
+const files = (dir) => readdirSync(dir).flatMap((n) => (statSync(join(dir, n)).isDirectory() ? files(join(dir, n)) : [join(dir, n)]));
+const fill = (text, shas) => text.replace(/\{\{(c\d+)(?::(\d+))?\}\}/g, (m, id, n) => {
+  if (!shas[id]) throw new Error(`placeholder ${m} names a commit that isn't made yet`);
+  return n ? shas[id].slice(0, Number(n)) : shas[id];
+});
+
+function place(from, root, rel, shas) {
+  const to = join(root, rel.replace(/\.fixture$/, ''));
+  mkdirSync(dirname(to), { recursive: true });
+  writeFileSync(to, fill(readFileSync(from, 'utf8'), shas));
+}
+
+export function replay(fixture, root, { trail = true } = {}) {
+  const spec = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(fixture, 'commits.json'), 'utf8'));
+  const git = (...a) => execFileSync('git', a, { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, GIT_AUTHOR_DATE: spec.date, GIT_COMMITTER_DATE: spec.date } }).trim();
+  mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
+  git('init', '-q', '-b', 'main');
+  git('config', 'user.email', 'fixture@example.com');
+  git('config', 'user.name', 'Fixture');
+  git('config', 'core.autocrlf', 'false');
+  cpSync(join(fixture, 'base'), root, { recursive: true });
+  git('add', '-A');
+  git('commit', '-q', '-m', 'base');
+  git('update-ref', 'refs/remotes/origin/main', 'HEAD');
+  git('checkout', '-q', '-b', spec.branch);
+  const shas = {};
+  for (const c of spec.commits) {
+    for (const rel of c.files) place(join(fixture, 'files', rel), root, rel, shas);
+    git('add', '-A');
+    const trailers = Object.entries(c.trailers).map(([k, v]) => `${k}: ${v}`).join('\n');
+    git('commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', c.subject, '-m', trailers);
+    shas[c.id] = git('rev-parse', 'HEAD');
+  }
+  if (trail && existsSync(join(fixture, 'trail'))) {
+    for (const f of files(join(fixture, 'trail'))) place(f, root, relative(join(fixture, 'trail'), f).replace(/\\/g, '/'), shas);
+  }
+  return { root, shas };
+}
